name: Arsenite Schism
summary: A split in the Byzantine church after Patriarch Arsenios excommunicated Emperor Michael VIII for blinding the boy emperor John IV, and was deposed for it; his followers refused communion with the official patriarchs for over 40 years.

start.label: Patriarch Arsenios excommunicates Michael VIII for blinding John IV

end.label: Arsenites reconciled with the official church under Andronikos II

key_dates.label: Arsenios deposed and exiled by a synod at Michael VIII's demand
Patriarch Joseph I absolves Michael VIII
Arsenios's remains brought back to Constantinople under Andronikos II

background.text: Michael VIII Palaiologos, co-emperor and regent for the child John IV Laskaris, recaptured Constantinople in 1261 and then had John IV, aged 11, blinded on Christmas Day 1261 to remove him as a rival.

happened.text: Patriarch Arsenios Autoreianos excommunicated Michael VIII for the crime.
Michael had a synod depose Arsenios in 1265 on charges including communion with the sultan of Iconium, and exiled him to the island of Proconnesus, where he died in 1273.
Many monks and laypeople, the 'Arsenites', refused to recognize his successors Germanos III and Joseph I, who absolved the emperor in 1267, and formed a separate party in church and politics.
The split overlapped with resistance to Michael VIII's union with Rome at the Second Council of Lyon (1274).

participants.name: Arsenios Autoreianos
participants.role: Patriarch of Constantinople who excommunicated the emperor

participants.name: Michael VIII Palaiologos
participants.role: Byzantine emperor who blinded John IV

participants.name: Andronikos II Palaiologos
participants.role: Emperor who worked to reconcile the Arsenites

outcomes.text: Andronikos II, Michael's son, brought Arsenios's remains back to the capital (1284), visited the blind John IV to seek forgiveness (1290), and finally reconciled the Arsenites in 1310.
The schism showed a patriarch using excommunication against an emperor and the emperor using a synod to remove him, a recurring pattern in Byzantium.

condemnations.reason: Michael VIII excommunicated for blinding John IV
condemnations.status: Lifted by Patriarch Joseph I in 1267 after the emperor did penance

condemnations.authority: Patriarchate of Constantinople, at the emperor's demand
condemnations.status: His memory was restored when his remains were honored in 1284

persecution.title: Blinding and imprisonment of John IV
persecution.summary: On Michael VIII's orders the 11-year-old emperor John IV Laskaris was blinded and imprisoned in a fortress in Bithynia, where he lived for decades.
persecution.outcome: John IV lived in confinement until about 1305.

persecution.title: Deposition and exile of Arsenios
persecution.summary: The patriarch was deposed by a synod packed with the emperor's supporters and exiled; Arsenite clergy and monks who refused communion with his successors were harassed, imprisoned, or exiled.
